transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-14
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Rossi (Aurora AI - Head of Product), Marcus Li (Aurora AI - ML Eng), Priya Menon (Aurora AI - CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): POC scope: run benchmark on 2GB sample, evaluate hosted vs Dedicated, verify function calling and structured JSON outputs, measure p50/p95 latency and per-token cost. Next steps include sharing SDK samples, pricing, and scheduling benchmark window.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we just wanted to kick off the scoping for the POC. I'll hand it over to Samir to run through the tech checklist but first quick intros?
[00:12] Elena Rossi: Hi, Elena here, Head of Product at Aurora, thanks for setting this up. We're looking to add more advanced summarization and tool-calling into our internal support product.
[00:21] Marcus Li: Marcus, ML, I will be doing the benchmarking and integration work on our side.
[00:26] Priya Menon: Priya, CTO, I'm here to cover timelines and security questions.
[00:31] Samir Patel: Great. So our goals today: align on success criteria — latency, cost, and output fidelity — plan benchmark inputs, and go over integration options: Node/Python SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and function/tool calling for structured output.
[00:45] Elena Rossi: For success criteria we care about p50 under 200ms for short summaries (<=256 tokens) and p95 below 600ms, cost target under $X per 1M tokens — we will share exact internal threshold after this meeting. Also need reliable structured JSON output for downstream ingestion.
[01:10] Samir Patel: Makes sense. Quick clarifier: when you say structured JSON, is that a fixed schema or more flexible key-value pairs?
[01:18] Elena Rossi: Mostly fixed schema — fields: issue_id, summary, severity, suggested_actions (list), and confidence. We need the model to validate and produce strict JSON ideally.
[01:27] Jamie Park: Redwood has two things that help here — our OpenAI-compatible endpoints support function calling/structured output, and we also run a structured-output postprocessor that can help enforce schema. There may be tradeoffs on latency if you add additional validations.
[01:46] Marcus Li: For workload sizing — our traffic is bursty. Typical steady qps is ~30 rps, peaks to 350 rps for 30-90 seconds. Average prompt length around 220 tokens, responses ~150 tokens. We'll provide a sample distribution.
[02:06] Samir Patel: Good — that distribution helps with batching and autoscaling config. For the POC we recommend a benchmark that covers steady-state at 30 rps, a medium spike at 120 rps and a peak window that hits 350 rps for a short duration.
[02:21] Priya Menon: On security: we require SOC 2 type II, customer-managed KMS for Private deployments, and audit logs retained for 90 days. Can Redwood support those for Dedicated or Private?
[02:34] Jamie Park: Yes — Dedicated and Private both support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. Hosted API also has SOC 2 but not customer-managed KMS unless you go to Private. We'll share the security pack.
[02:46] Elena Rossi: We're leaning hosted for speed of onboarding but concerned about the data residency and KMS.
[02:51] Jamie Park: Totally fair. For the POC we can run benchmarks on Hosted with a pseudonymized dataset, and if results look good we can pilot Dedicated with KMS for the production rollout.
[03:05] Marcus Li: Can you detail the SDK support? We use Node serverless backend and some Python microservices. We also call the API via an internal gateway — we want OpenAI-compatible endpoints to minimize changes.
[03:17] Samir Patel: We have official Node and Python SDKs; both offer the same OpenAI-compatible request shapes and have a function-calling wrapper. Example: you can send a functions array similar to OpenAI and get typed JSON back. We'll share snippets after the call. There's also a streaming SDK for lower-latency tail responses.
[03:36] Marcus Li: Any differences between Hosted and Dedicated in terms of endpoint compatibility?
[03:41] Samir Patel: None on API shape — same OpenAI-compatible endpoints across modes, the differences are runtime knobs: batch sizes, kv-cache hot warm configs, and autoscaling behavior. Those are configurable for Dedicated.
[03:55] Elena Rossi: About benchmarks — we want to validate p50/p95, token cost, and correctness for structured outputs. Can Redwood run multi-run benchmarks or do we need to run them on our infra?
[04:07] Samir Patel: We can run the benchmark on Redwood's hosted infra as a first pass — we configure the workload generator with your prompts and sample dataset. For Dedicated validation we typically run a 48-hour benchmark on a dedicated pool to capture autoscale behavior.
[04:20] Jamie Park: We'll need your sample prompts and a representative dataset — Marcus mentioned ~2GB — and metadata on concurrency patterns. Provide those as a signed S3 link and an account contact.
[04:32] Marcus Li: We'll upload the data. For metrics, we want p50/p95 percentiles, 99th tail, error rates, and cost per 1M tokens. Also throughput and GPU utilization if possible.
[04:45] Samir Patel: We'll capture all of that; we'll also include per-token breakdown and model variant comparisons (quantized vs full float) if you want. That helps with cost projections.
[04:57] Priya Menon: How do you handle function calling failures or schema drift — if the model outputs invalid JSON?
[05:05] Samir Patel: Good Q. Function calling is often reliable but we recommend a two-tier approach: 1) use the built-in function-calling/structured mode to bias outputs toward schema, 2) run an optional lightweight schema validator (we can host or you can run) to catch/repair outputs. For high-safety pipelines we recommend the validator plus a fallback route that hits a more deterministic model.
[05:29] Elena Rossi: That fallback flow sounds important. How much extra latency would schema validation add?
[05:34] Samir Patel: If done inline on the same request it adds minimal latency for small schemas — single-digit ms. If you do a reparsing/second-call flow it could add 100–300ms depending on payload and model. We'll show numbers in the benchmark.
[05:48] Marcus Li: For latency SLOs is it realistic to get p95 <600ms on Hosted at peak load for our prompt sizes?
[05:56] Samir Patel: For short responses and with proper batching and KV cache warm, yes it's realistic on Dedicated and often achievable on Hosted for moderate peaks. At extreme peaks (350 rps sustained) Dedicated with reserved GPU pools is more predictable.
[06:10] Jamie Park: One practical note — when you use OpenAI-compatible calls, make sure your retry/timeout logic maps to Redwood SLOs. We'll share best-practice client configs.
[06:20] Elena Rossi: Ok, timeline — we'd like a 2-3 week POC with benchmarks and final decision by mid-September. Is that doable?
[06:28] Jamie Park: Yes. Proposed schedule: week of 8/18: exchange datasets & success criteria; week of 8/26: run 48-hour benchmark; 9/02 review + results; decision by 9/12. Does that align?
[06:40] Priya Menon: That works but need security review in parallel — can you share SOC 2 and KMS docs by 8/16?
[06:47] Jamie Park: We'll send the security pack by tomorrow and the KMS onboarding doc by 8/16.
[06:52] Marcus Li: On the integration side, can you show an example of a function-calling payload and a Node snippet to validate the JSON?
[06:59] Samir Patel: Absolutely — snippet will include functions schema, call shape, and a streaming example for low-latency responses. I'll include Python and Node versions.
[07:10] Elena Rossi: One more thing — can Redwood emit typed structured outputs for downstream ingestion? We prefer not to do heavy parsing on our side.
[07:17] Samir Patel: Yes, we can return strict JSON or a top-level envelope. For more robust guarantees we'll do function-calling plus the optional postprocessing step. We can also provide a small SDK helper that validates and repairs common issues.
[07:30] Jamie Park: Great. Quick recap of next steps then: Redwood send pricing & security docs; Samir send SDK examples and function-calling snippets; Aurora to upload dataset and confirm success criteria; schedule benchmark week of 8/26; follow-up review 9/02.
[07:47] Elena Rossi: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:51] Priya Menon: Thanks.
[07:54] Jamie Park: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the links and notes.

End of transcript.
